supported_facts.fact: COSX grid2 is used through SCF convergence; grid3 is used for final energy and gradient evaluation. GridX/IntAccX control these grids. UseFinalGridX can disable the final grid, but the manual generally discourages changing it.

Since ORCA6, COSX analytic derivatives include grid-weight and fitting-matrix derivatives. The manual describes improved energy/gradient consistency, so a blanket claim that final COSX gradients are omitted is unsupported.

DEFGRID3 uses XC angular grid6 and COSX angular grids2,3,4. AngularGridX and IntAccX expose angular and radial controls; equal angular labels alone do not document equal complete integration settings.

External point charges contribute to the one-electron matrix and nuclear interaction. Their mutual interaction is excluded for external files unless DoEQ enables it; this supports retaining the existing DoEQ=false/MM bookkeeping.

VeryTightSCF uses ConvCheckMode2. Native convergence therefore does not imply every printed density/DIIS criterion passes. ConvCheckMode0 is stricter but has documented exceptions when other criteria are overachieved.
ConvForced controls subsequent work on nonconverged wavefunctions; it is not an all-residual convergence selector. SCF convergence also does not establish electronic stability.

inference.label: Scientific interpretation, not an explicit pcgrad implementation guarantee from the manual.
inference.statement: A density stationary for the grid2 energy need not be stationary for grid3. Displacing an external charge changes the density at fixed QM coordinates, so the post-SCF correction can have a density-response derivative. Saved decomposition can implicate this correction without identifying an omitted implementation term.

unknowns_and_limits: The consulted primary documentation does not explicitly guarantee whether external .pcgrad includes every density-response term associated with the post-SCF grid3 correction.
General RIJCOSX gradient documentation is not proof of pcgrad-specific handling, nor proof that pcgrad is defective.
No source-code implementation was available for this check. No missing-response term or causal bug is established.
SCF paths, runtime differences and single-step truncation remain distinct unresolved possibilities unless actual saved evidence or separately declared qualification resolves them.

conditional_three_cell_proposal.trigger: Consider only after actual saved decomposition implicates the final-grid correction.
conditional_three_cell_proposal.question: Does matching the integration used for density convergence and final evaluation restore the declared external-charge directional derivative agreement?
conditional_three_cell_proposal.single_candidate: Predeclare one matched angular/radial grid2=grid3 configuration, retaining modern COSX gradient/fitting treatment; verify executed settings in native output. This is not a settings sweep.
cells: One central analytic-gradient calculation including native external point-charge gradient
One plus singlepoint at original h=0.001A
One minus singlepoint at original h=0.001A
conditional_three_cell_proposal.matched_scope: All three use the same state, geometry definitions, charge field lineage, numerical recipe and runtime allocation policy; only the declared displacement and energy/gradient run type differ.
conditional_three_cell_proposal.comparison: Use the new matching central gradient and both new endpoint energies. Keep original derivative tolerance and component/state admissions; record all printed residuals and final-grid corrections.
conditional_three_cell_proposal.limits: Three cells establish agreement only at the declared step. Any step-stability extension must be separately bounded before execution. Old failed endpoints/gradient remain immutable; no retrospective gate relaxation.
conditional_three_cell_proposal.continuation: Original failed scout remains failed. Remaining six derivative points and eight response endpoints remain stopped under the original protocol; a new proposal alone does not reopen them.
